Recent advances in source segmentation have significantly benefited various self-supervised image processing tasks, including video processing. To effectively utilize these improvements for video processing, our research uses the Source-Separation task with color image demosaicing and compressive video reconstruction models. Selecting the most effective algorithms from a diverse range of source segmentation methods proved to be a challenging task. An initial approach utilizing source mask reconstruction loss led to inconsistent results and instability across various iterations. Ultimately, an indicator based on gradient descent steps proved to be the most effective source algorithm choice criterion, achieving state-of-the-art performance in multiple tasks. For image demosaicing, our method reached comparable or superior results to current leading approaches. Ten sources were consistently utilized, particularly fnet and Cra, delivering excellent outcomes. When ten sources were employed, our method achieved the lowest average PSNR and SSIM values of 34.06 dB, 0.91 respectively, outperforming the Compressive Video Restoration baselines of 33.78 dB, 0.90 obtained through direct usage of previous baselines.

This paper explores the effects of randomized geometry on the dynamics of incompressible polar active fluids in the context of a Tulip model, displaying a non-trivial "glassy" state after incomepressibility is imposed. By using dimensionless parameters, we examined the flow patterns and structural properties of the system's dynamics across different spatial dimensions ($d=3$ to $d=8$) by employing direct simulation Monte Carlo methods. Our studies revealed an intricate relationship between the dimensions and average flow patterns, as well as a sudden and notable occurrence of vortex formation in three-dimensional space that gradually diminishes with increasing dimensions. We also investigated the scaling behavior of density fluctuations, which indicate a form of long-range correlation in lower dimensions that disappears beyond eight dimensions. Notably, we observed that the structural dynamics adhere to a modified form of the Rayleigh-Taylor theorem, scaled to the spatial dimensions of the system.

Optical character recognition (OCR) systems often produce inaccurate results when translating image texts into digital format, frequently requiring manual correction due to their inability to accurately reflect data from real-world documents. To address this issue, this research explores the integration of natural language processing (NLP) techniques to produce a more robust and efficient Indonesian ID document extractor. The proposed method combines an adaptive threshold-based morphological operation with Tesseract OCR for color segmentations and text extraction from colored Indonesian ID documents. A CTAN package called `structure` is utilized to analyze the document's structure, while RNN-based part-of-speech tagging helps in interpreting the extracted text. The proposed method is evaluated using 500 Indonesian ID documents, demonstrating high extraction completeness and interpretation accuracy compared to traditional approaches. The extraction completeness is measured at 97.2%, while the interpretation accuracy is assessed at 97%.

A propelled harmonic oscillator under going through a time-varying potential, characterized by frequency and phase parameters in both inner and outer loops, was thoroughly investigated in the current study. Analytical solutions were derived for several scenarios involving linear and nonlinear driving forces. Furthermore, quantum states were identified that remain unchanged over time. The application of the path integral technique was demonstrated to obtain propagators and probability distributions. Furthermore, the propagator was calculated for the harmonic oscillator in the presence of a time-varying driving force. The propagator was utilized to obtain the time-dependent probability distribution of a particle's position. Both Monte Carlo simulations and Metropolis algorithms were employed to compute path integrals to obtain probability distributions. The results indicate that analytical and numerical methods yield nearly identical probability distributions.

The YORP effect has received considerable interest in recent years as it causes the gradual alteration of small asteroid physical properties over time. To uncover its effects on particular asteroids, shape models and light curves, obtained from different viewing angles, are essential to estimate their spin rates and detect any changes. In the case of asteroids (10115) 1992 SK, (1685) Toro, and (1620) Geographos, high-precision light curves were analyzed to complement existing data from various sources, including radar observations and optical imaging, as well as space-based observations of Geographos. Furthermore, the integration of the YORP model allowed researchers to consider potential variations in rotation rates. By combining all available data and solving the light curve simultaneously with the YORP model, more accurate results were achieved compared to previous studies that relied on solving the YORP equation. However, no significant variations in semi-diurnal periods were detected for these asteroids during the observed time span, although theoretical predictions suggest a gradual shortening of days due to the YORP effect is inevitable.

We demonstrate that non-Heisenstein property of a collection of surface group representations is equivalent to the topological compactness of its Topo-character variety under the Rosendal-topology. Additionally, if a collection of surface homeomorphisms is topologically precompact, we prove it must contain a finite number of realizations of distinct semi-simple actions, possibly shifted by commutators of certain curves. Furthermore, if a collection of surface homeomorphisms is non-Topo-precompact, we establish there exists a closed curve whose winding numbers differ by at least 1 for some pairs of homeomorphisms within the collection.

The SMT solver Par1 can handle theories of arrays and linear arithmetic, and has been employed in automated theorem proving and software testing. However, it lacks support for handling infinite sequences, which are integral to software analysis, particularly in the context of program verification and refinement. To address this limitation, we developed an extension to Par1 that enables the handling of executable infinite sequences. This extension allows for the resolution of questions regarding the existence of solutions to systems of equations with infinite sequences within the scope of linear arithmetic. We implemented this extension as a Pluggable Parser for the Par1 language, and used it to prove the existence of infinite sequences that satisfy certain conditions. Additionally, we examined the computational complexity of this problem and established both upper and lower bounds. This research can be accessed on ArXiv under the number 2006.08554.

Agent-based models are widely used to replicate complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components, however simulating these models behind the scenes can be computationally intensive for large-scale interactions. A new approach is presented here to infer the underlying rules of unknown coexisting agent types in one-dimensional non-equilibrium systems. Our method is based on an analysis of the statistical behavior observed in the system, without requiring access to the underlying particle dynamics or prior knowledge of the interaction rules. This approach infers inter-particle interactions and initial speed distributions from empirical data on macroscopic densities, currents, and local densities by combining exploratory data manipulation, artificial intelligence, and matrix theory. This method successfully identifies the coexisting 'slow' and 'fast' puller types with different interaction rules and speed distributions, and also distinguishes between similar models such as TASEP and NTASEP. A likely explanation for the simultaneous existence of fast and slow particles with specific interaction patterns is put forward, and the approach presented here is found to offer a general and effective means of uncovering the underlying nature of multiple simultaneous hidden species in non-equilibrium systems.

The attainable set of a differential game represents the collection of points that can reach their destination within a specified time frame from a given initial point. For dynamic systems, determining the boundary of an attainable set is crucial for establishing effective control measures and risk management strategies. A study focuses on a particular variant of a differential game to compute an explicit representation of the attainable set in its second-order form, based on a connection with the boundary control case of a variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, which can be described as a second-order nonconvex Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation with Discontinuous Hamiltonian. This research develops a numerical approach to calculate the necessary components and the boundary of an attainable set at any given time, given an initial condition, and validates the accuracy of this method through numerical examples.

The ventral temporal cortex (VTC) is a brain region where stimuli containing people are given special treatment and given a higher-level category called the animacy exception to a general rule.  Recent studies have shown that this animacy exception to the rule is linked to how quickly the brain processes information, but it remains unclear if this is because of the presence of people or simply because of over-generalizing this feature.  To address this issue, we used a new type of experimental design that combined continuous information processing measures with model-based analysis to test two possible explanations: whether the animacy exception to the rule is because of the presence of people or because of extending this feature to a broader category.  By using a large set of stimuli including inanimate objects with a similar property called "agency", we discovered that the animacy exception to the rule is actually due to the presence of people, not because of extending this feature to a broader category.  This finding has significant implications for understanding the functional role of the part of the VTC that responds to stimuli containing people.

A quantum unique ergodicity (QUHe) conjecture posits that a specific family of holomorphic and non-holomorphic modular forms becomes asymptotically orthogonal as their weight increases. A previous proof by Soundararajan and Templiner established this behavior for the family, but their efficient variance bound required a significant variance reduction to achieve the desired result. A key challenge in tackling the QUHe problem within the Maass setting is obtaining an exceptional DSR bound with minimal impact on variance computation. While existing various bound estimates provide some progress, they fall short of meeting minimal requirements. However, our research presents a more effective various bound computation for the family of classical Dirichlet L-functions, establishing an improved result with minimal overhead. Specifically, we replicated and re-established a non-trivial aspect of the QUHe proof for complex valued L-functions, effectively generalizing a previous, more limited proof. As consequences of our various bound computation, we also established related asymptotic uncorrelatedness properties, effectively extending previous, limited results.

We introduce the Quantum Relational Hoare Framework with Anticipations, a novel substructure of the quantum relational hoart, which enables the anticipation of preconditions and postconditions in programs. This substructure facilitates a more efficient generation of program anticipations. We also define the concepts of quantum anticipation laws and anticipate programs. Additionally, we develop the main theorem of quantum anticipation. To illustrate the main results, we provide a collection of examples. All proofs can be found in the appendix.

The phenomenon of "super-spreading" has been observed in various contexts, including everyday life and significant events like the COVID-19 pandemic, and also in animal-to-animal transmission and deadlier animal plagues. A key characteristic of these outbreaks is skewed transmission that results from a small number of highly infectious events. Although this paper delves into the effects of such occurrences within modeled epidemics, there's still a need for comprehensive statistical analyses of infectious disease data to fully understand "super-spreading" dynamics. We employed an agent-based model, complete with data from synthetic outbreaks to explore how "super-spreading" events, in various proportions, influence the course of an epidemic, as well as the resulting plagues, in terms of characteristics such as mortality curves, pandemic severity, and growth and decline rates. The study reveals that models exhibiting "super-spreading" events lead to larger initial outbreaks and more intense plagues, as well as models with multiple phases of infection transmission. Furthermore, this paper presents novel approaches to model time-dependent vaccination rates and reveals that "super-spreading" events, in combination with these methods, significantly influence the dynamics of a pandemic, including the rate of its spread and duration.

The concept of stability in control theory relies on the codiskcyclicity of an operator, which is further explored in this paper. We define a generalised sense of codiskcyclicity for operators acting on the topological vector spaces that contain the space of continuous functions defined on a compact set $p$. If an operator is codiskcyclic in this sense, it implies that the components of any target function within a specific subset of $p$ can be accurately predicted by linear combinations of observations of the input data. It's also proven that a target function within $p$ is perfectly reconstructible from observations of another function, provided the latter is odiskcyclic with respect to a specific subset of $p$. The criteria for a tuple of mutually codiskcyclic operators to exist, are examined across various subsets of $p$, including those with a measure and those consisting of discrete data points. Furthermore, the relationship between codiskcyclicity and the cyclicity of the adjoint operators is established.

Direct current (DC) measurements provide a reliable reference for assessing imaging techniques used to measure vector magnetic fields, particularly in high-frequency measurements of magnetic fields projected onto the solar surface through various instruments like magnetographs and occulmeters. This study systematically evaluates a compilation of conversion algorithms employed to derive line-of-sight magnetic fields from interferometric measurements, considering various input data sets characterized by differing spatial resolutions, signal-to-noise ratios, and Stokes parameter asymmetries, which can indicate intrinsic or instrumental asymmetries that may skew results. A prominent issue of asymmetry in the Stokes $V$ signal was discovered, which, if uncorrected, can significantly distort vector magnetic field estimates in accordance with the strong-field approximation, leading to substantial biases in derived parameters such as magnetic field strength, helicity, and asymmetry. It is essential to address this problem to accurately measure these parameters from derived measurements. Furthermore, a straightforward post-processing method was developed to mitigate this asymmetry by adjusting synthetic Stokes $V$ profiles based on the corresponding Doppler velocity, which, despite introducing vector magnetic field estimates that are generally within a factor of two of the true values, demonstrates substantial variability among different inversion codes and highlights the necessity for continued, large-scale, systematic comparisons to enhance and standardize the accuracy of these techniques.

A sign dilemma in Monte Carlo simulations involving the Hubbard model is addressed by a novel complex-valued neural network ansatz for the ground-state wavefunction. 
In contrast to a real-valued PFACK reference function, our design omits the sign dilemma entirely. 
Our approach's simplicity leads to an uncomplicated training procedure, even at a low temperature where the system exhibits characteristic Fermi-Dirac distribution. 
Our finding that a complex phase component of the neural network remains largely constant underscores the sign function's inherent positive nature, leading to an entirely complex-valued wavefunction.

This research investigates how topological entropy and factor complexity behave when free group generators are added or removed, and when morphisms are applied to free groups. We establish that for a reduced sub-free group subgroup defined within the stable letter free group, the topological entropy of a letter mapping decreases proportionally to the reduced subgroup's length, and the factor complexity of a factor map also declines. Moreover, we demonstrate that a letter mapping reduces the topological complexity of a word directly, and the factor complexity of a word also decreases when applied. These findings correspond to previously observed behaviors in free group automorphisms related to stabilization and change of basis laws. Additionally, we examine how these properties change under semi-direct product constructions and provide a modified upper bound for the factor complexity of retree automata.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting to new tasks without explicit guidance, unsupervised cross-task generalization is a key area of research.
This paper introduces a novel unsupervised cross-task generalization approach called Retrieval Enhancement, which utilizes past knowledge to select and combine relevant segments from existing texts in the target domain.
In an iterative, online setting, we incorporate adaptive priorities to better reflect the current needs of the application at hand.
In unsupervised tests for news title generation, our results show significant improvements over standard approaches when dealing with unfamiliar topics, particularly those not already present in the training data.

Machine learning models, including those based on artificial neural networks, are highly sensitive to privacy breaches due to their memorization tendency. The risk of revealing sensitive data can be significantly minimized by training models that conform to differential privacy. However, this innovative approach requires a thorough investigation of its performance optimization methods, particularly in the context of typical neural network training processes. A significant hurdle in optimizing hyperparameters for algorithms ensuring privacy lies in memeorizability's intricate nature, coupled with assessing an individual's influence on generalizability leading to potential bias towards models with lower security. This study aims to overcome these challenges by utilizing a novel framework that employs gradient inversion to evaluate a model's tendency to memorize data, thereby facilitating an efficient tuning procedure for crucial hyperparameters. The proposed method achieved successful results in optimizing vital neural network hyperparameters, yielding a notable enhancement in balancing the balance between model accuracy and data privacy, particularly in relation to previously established methods.

In the context of learning ordered data structures, researchers are examining involutions as a group. Currently, no ordered structure has been established for the complex of involutions, except for the inclusion relationship, in an attempt to define more comprehensive structures. This study implements various ordered structures, including the suffix order, which results in a double ordering when combined with its opposite, and explores the implications of these involutions on educational and biological sequence analysis.

To better understand galaxy evolution, a comprehensive map of the chemical elements in stars is essential. A new statistical model has been developed with the assistance of the APOGEE-2 database to clarify the metallicity distribution in the Milky Way's disk. This model, consisting of two correlated components, is primarily governed by a metallicity threshold at the $-0.6$ decile, and is further differentiated by spin, allowing the identification of thick and thin disks through residual abundances. The study of this model's behavior reveals distinct patterns in the distribution of stars within the galaxy, and the residual abundances are found to be closely correlated with specific chemical elements and stellar spin. These residual abundances are thought to be a result of the star formation history, stellar feedback, and supernova contributions in the galaxy.

While previous studies have delved into COVID-19 misinformation's consequences, little attention has been paid to its dissemination dynamics. This research investigates how misinformation spreads in news headlines during China's COVID-19 outbreak, formulating a mechanism for its propagation and measuring its impact. A content-based approach was employed to track the spread of misinformation across news headlines at the national level, with a statistical model used to assess how misinformation-related attention affected stock prices in the Chinese finance market. A key finding is that rumors peak within the early stages of an epidemic and then stabilize. Additionally, areas with high population density and a high proportion of urban residents were discovered to accelerate the spread of misinformation. Finally, our analysis indicates that stock prices in affected regions were influenced by local rumors, with no evidence of them spreading uniformly.

A comprehensive study of the galaxies within the Fornax cluster can be significantly advanced by analyzing the planetary nebulae they contain, whose light serves as a precise indicator of their parent galaxy's intrinsic brightness. To further push the boundaries of local cosmology research, it is essential to develop an efficient method for measuring intrinsic brightness in a automated manner. This requires a in-depth analysis of the planetary nebulae that are located within these galaxies. The Furnace3D project, whose scope involves analyzing the planetary nebulae within the galaxies of the Fornax cluster, continues its research with the incorporation of three key components: an examination of the Milky Way, the Sculptor cluster, and the Centaurus cluster, along with analyzing early-type and luminous galaxies, as well as presenting the Planetary Nebulae Directory for the Fornax Cluster (FND3P), which maps the location of over 140,000 planetary nebulae within the Fornax cluster's galaxies using a consistent set of observational parameters from six different telescopes. Furthermore, the FND3P comes with a framework for determining the intrinsic brightness of the galaxies in an entirely automated manner, which serves as a precise distance-measuring tool. Its effectiveness has been proven through a case study of the angular momentum galaxies, demonstrating its capability for measuring distances and yielding a result of 19.7 (+2/-1) Mpc, which aligns with the consensus of the cluster's location.

Traditional analytical engines struggle with efficiency when handling sequential data, prompting the need for a engine that excels in both fixed queries and regular data analysis. A novel approach is introduced in this study, focusing on preserving data integrity during vector operations, enabling the blending of arithmetic operations with tree traversal operations, and facilitating a high degree of optimization. A resulting architecture, termed "LifeFlow," combines data structures and vector operations, circulates within a closed loop, and is optimized for high-speed processing using GPU technology. LifeFlow features an innovative row-tight storage method, a circular data flow design, and the elimination of index translation and data array operations. A real-world application, utilizing URL shortening services, demonstrates the exceptional performance of LifeFlow, exhibiting a 33-fold speed increase over SQL and the elimination of B+ tree in the data structure, and outperforming Go routines in language, with a 2-fold speed increase in language and a 55-fold speed increase in language+database, and eliminating the use of Redis in the system.

This research paper confirms a previous counter-example, demonstrating that all Berland curves in certain types of space-time environments include timelike spiral curves. It also provides specific examples of environments where timelike Berlad curves exist and × 3, but not environments where double warped product Minkowski spaces would occur.

The choice of loss function in supervised learning, particularly for classification, is a crucial decision. Although the foundational loss functions, such as cross-entropy, are widely used, numerous alternatives exist. Despite its significance, loss function selection often lacks thorough exploration and theoretical underpinnings. This is especially evident in the context of deep learning. Our extensive experimental underkilling dataset comprises 500 tasks across five different deep learning frameworks. This large-scale examination enables more informed conclusions. In an attempt to expand our findings, we also examined five different model architectures in an attempt to broaden our results.

This research focuses on the rapid structural changes that occur when 
strain-induced crystallization happens, particularly in the molecular and 
micro-mechanical aspects of rubber materials. To effectively simulate these 
structural developments, a new numerical method has been devised based on the 
heat equation's coupling with a structural equation, which accounts for 
convection caused by temperature-dependent material properties and latent 
heat, along with a simulation of material deformation's impact on a finite 
element mesh. When applied to both numerical tests and actual experiments 
involving sudden stretching of latex, this integrated approach successfully 
captures the crystallization, convection, and local mesh distortion, leading 
to the formation of elongated, triangular shapes within the material.

To better fully describe the paramagnetic response to an external magnetic field applied perpendicular to a nematic superconductor's symmetry plane, a theoretical framework was developed. Analytical expressions for the magnetic response can be derived within the Fumi gas model. Furthermore, this approach allows us to incorporate the impact of superconductor thickness. Computational results show that the magnetic response to an infinite thickness superconductor can be directly applied to thin-film samples. Additionally, we discovered that for perpendicular magnetic fields, the Pauli paramagnetic response of Cooper pairs in the triplet state is a crucial component. This is in contrast to Type-I and Anderson triplet states, where the Pauli response of Cooper pairs is negligible.

A newly proposed differential detection method, a modification of traditional techniques, offers improved performance for a wide range of differential detection schemes. The key improvement lies in a strategy to minimize noise impact by utilizing samples from adjacent time periods. In an ideal scenario, this approach can achieve a 3dB signal-to-noise ratio compared to conventional methods. Theoretical analysis and computer simulations confirm that the noise reduction achieved varies depending on the detection parameters, with minimal performance loss in most cases. The 3dB improvement is observed in specific parameter settings.

The research reveals that the quantum potential of the universe's vacuum could be equivalent to the energy density required for dark energy. Current large language models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable inferential abilities, yet they struggle with consistency in their reasoning, a issue known as stochasticity. To address this problem in the domain of causal reasoning, we introduce an rule-based approach that leverages the concept of machine common knowledge in the form of a knowledge atlas. Inspired by van Kempen's framework, our approach, called ATOMIC, constructs an atlas of machine common knowledge consisting of approximately 1.2 million "if-then" rules. This atlas is generated through a knowledge distillation process from stochastic LLMs and encompasses a diverse range of domains. When a participant question is passed to our model, it applies the relevant "if-then" rules from the atlas to derive its answer, a process called an atlas-based inference. Through rigorous testing, we discovered that current LLMs readily incorporate the ATOMIC atlas, yielding a 61% reduction in reasoning stochasticity and a 18% improvement in accuracy on the CausalIQ benchmark.

In the NISQ era, it is crucial to take advantage of the coming advent of practical full-scale quantum computers within the next few years. To achieve this, it is essential to utilize nearby quantum hardware effectively and plan investments in short-term quantum markets accordingly. We are introducing a variant of the Hazan-Hartglia algorithm from 2020, renaming it NISQ-HHL to accommodate the needs of short-term quantum markets. The original Hazan-Hartglia hybrid approach, designed for high-scale classical and quantum computers in 2020, is being adapted for use with short-term quantum devices. NISQ-HHL is able to execute the HHL part of the original algorithm seamlessly on short-term quantum devices. The results obtained from NISQ-HHL show superior performance compared to the MH-Haz, a hybrid approach utilizing Monte-Halting sampling and the Hazan-Hartglia method, particularly in terms of risk-adjusted returns. The NISQ-HHL approach also manages to produce results with higher feasibility on the actual quantum hardware.

To improve speech assistance systems, especially in terms of spoken answer formulation, this study formulates two primary challenges and addresses them with an innovative multi-modal training approach. The first challenge is developing a robust method to integrate audio transcripts and text content in a unified neural network, which our solution - bidirectional attention filter (BAF) - accomplishes with selective multi-modal input processing. The second challenge involves synchronizing the BAF's hidden representations with data from both sources, which is tackled using a multi-task neural network. Our method eliminates the need for complex alignment mechanisms commonly employed in such integrations. Experimentation with two distinct datasets, specifically the Librispeech corpus, demonstrates our method's efficacy, yielding a 8.4% reduction in word error rate (WER) compared to a baseline, along with improved performance on additional validation and test sets. Furthermore, our model exhibits superior accuracy in tasks requiring speech-based understanding.

This paper paper investigates limited-position drivers in a probabilistic model of uniform random parking functions. We establish that, for a uniformly random parking function of length n, the number of cars positioned at the beginning is approximately $ \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} $, and for any integer k greater than one, the expected number of cars positioned at the beginning is $ k+1 $. We also provide further results and directions for research.

The thin-superconductor film's Meissner effect can be disrupted by patterned substrate below a critical width, leading to the formation of nanowires with accessible quantum phase of electrons. As a result, the Josephson effect dominates the electron transport through these nanowires, allowing for a gate-voltage-controlled conductance coherent oscillations in the nanowires made from NbN material. Nonetheless, studies on thin-superconductor films and nanowires contradict each other; whereas former show no missing zero-voltage peak in I-V curves, the latter involve Coherent oscillations. To address this issue, we conducted an in-depth investigation into the conductance of NbN nanowires and found that nanowire fabrication process causes a combination of the quantum interference and the Coulomb blockade effect. As a result, the result is a pattern that resembles a "checkboard" in the gate-voltage space; in some nanowire segments, the conductance is in a state of blockade, in others it is in a state of oscillation. To predict future videos from current footage, particularly in underrepresented areas, our novel approach involves a dual neural network structure. One part of this system uses a generic video event predictor trained on vast datasets, while the other part is tailored to specific videos with unusual elements. We believe this method is beneficial given the common presence of unique features in real-world videos and leverages powerful, pre-trained models. Our experiments show that our system excels at predicting future videos, especially in scenes containing unique elements, and demonstrates success across various test scenarios.

Correlations between electrons in different atomic orbitals are key to comprehending various physical phenomena in elements and compounds, yet they are difficult to measure directly. Using a highly sensitive technique to detect electron distances, researchers have investigated single electrons situated in different orbitals within a hydrogen atom. As the inter-electronic separation increases, evidence for inter-orbital interaction emerges and aligns with predictions from quantum mechanics.

The Ω-baryon, possessing three s quarks and exhibiting negative parity, is anticipated to exhibit multiple excited states through theoretical calculation.
However, due to its notably low production cross-section in hadron collisions, experimental research into this particle has been limited to mostly upper mass limits.
This work presents the first direct observation of the Ω-baryon, achieved by analyzing a dataset from p-Pb collisions at various centrality levels recorded by the ALICE detector at the LHC.
By examining three decay channels of the first excited state of the Ω-baryon with -1,-1,-1 and examining the kaon multiplicity, three distinct methods of analysis were employed to determine the particle's mass.
Through fitting of invariant mass distributions, no resonant signal was detected in any of the Ω-baryon decay channels under investigation.
As a result, new upper limits on the total cross-sections of the Ω-baryon were established for the first time, ranging from 744 nb to 2.466 pb depending on the specific collision centrality.

Epidemics transmitted through the air, like COVID- public health forecasting through air-borne transmission necessitates an accurate model of air-borne transmission itself, which in turn depends on the distribution of infectious and susceptible individuals within the given space. Agent-based models (ABM) are well-suited to provide a precise description of spatial transmission given their long-standing success in forecasting building ventilation performance. We assess the efficacy of using ABM to predict COVID-19 transmission on a bus, first validating our model's ability to accurately forecast air-borne transmission, and then exploring the benefits of using ABM over simpler, statistically-based regression models. By leveraging the fully observable nature of a specific bus and extensively simulated time-series data, we find that a well-mixed ABM framework yields significant benefits in forecasting accuracy, primarily due to its ability to account for the transmission dynamics affecting the spread of COVID-19. Furthermore, we demonstrate that even with limited data availability, a ABM framework can effectively forecast COVID-19 transmission on a bus.

Bi-based materials exhibit exceptionally large spin-orbit coupling, making them valuable for researching various spin-dependent phenomena and having potential applications in devices. When Bi layers are combined with ferromagnetic layers, the spin-orbit proximity effect Bi induces modifies the Co's intrinsic low spin-orbit coupling properties. However, instances of this effect have so far been rare. This study explores the spin-orbit proximity effect on Bi/Co multilayers, investigating how interfacial interactions affect the anomalous Hall effect. Findings reveal that the modified intrinsic Hall angle in the Co layers occurs as a result of enhanced spin-helical states created by strong spin-orbit coupling at the interface. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the magnitude of this effect is influenced by the thickness of the Bi layers and the direction in which the multilayer is deposited, indicating that spin-helical state behavior results from increased backward electron flow. In addition to quantifying the spin-orbit proximity effect, it also highlights the role of backscattering at the interface in transmitting spin-helical states to the adjacent Co layers. Bi/Co multilayers exhibit diverse applications and are thus an ideal subject for examining interfacial modifications.

This study presents the analytic solution to the time-independent fractional Schrödinger equation in $d$ dimensions, when acted upon by a generalized Mie-type potential, and offers a corresponding energy spectrum expression. Additionally, it derives the appropriate condition for the normalizability of the wave function. Furthermore, explicit expressions for the fractional expectation values of the radial distance are derived. A key feature of this research is that it provides a fractional approach to a broad spectrum of potential fields that include the Coulomb, Lennard-Jones (12-8), and Mieshchshkoff (6-8) potentials as subcategories. Moreover, it delivers a non-relativistic quantum mechanics solution to an $d$-dimensional harmonic oscillator within a fractional framework. Notably, this research is applicable in the contexts of non-Newtonian dynamics and anomalous quantum dynamics.

A approach called "Lipschitz consistency" training is proposed to deeply train neural networks, drawing inspiration from the concept of preserving local neighborhoods under network transformations. This method addresses the limitation of traditional networks that may overfit and fails to generalize effectively. By integrating a penalty term into the standard loss function, we enforce a bound on the network's Lipschitz constant, thereby improving generalization performance. Unlike other approaches, our consistency loss does not require a reference distribution or the training of an additional inverse network. Instead, we randomly sample pairs of inputs from the training data, a strategy known as "data pair regularization". We analyze the relationship between our approach and other forms of regularization, and demonstrate the superiority of our method over existing techniques. Experimental results using various architectures and datasets, such as CIFAR10/100 and ImageNet, indicate that incorporating our proposed "Lipschitz consistency" loss yields a 10% enhancement in test accuracy.

We investigate the Drell-Yan production of colorless vector leptoquarks at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the 8 TeV LHC 8 TeV and take into consideration all relevant NLO QCD corrections, drawn from existing literature. Our research reveals that, for certain types of third-generation vector leptoquarks, the total cross-section for direct production can be comparable to, or even exceed, the combined cross-section for associated production with bottom-quarks. Consequently, the discovery of a single decay of charged leptoquarks into hadrons could lead to an estimation of its mass. If the leptoquarks' mass exceeds approximately 700-900 GeV, associated production with bottom-quarks becomes the primary creation method. Our research also provides new results on the associated production of semi-neutral leptoquarks at the LHC 8 TeV.

Radiation risks associated with Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scans are significant, particularly when they are frequent, as in scenarios like disease monitoring. To minimize these effects, low-dose PET imaging is being investigated. To achieve better images at lower doses, a neural network was developed to transform a high-quality PET scan into a lower-dose PET scan, thereby preserving detailed features. This study employs a unique, innovative, and dual-fold neural network architecture, comprising an encoder-decoder network paired with a generator, both utilizing different neural elements, to simultaneously reconstruct images and distinguish between high- and low-dose images. To further enhance performance, a novel, unified loss function was created that combines multiple assessment methods into one, simultaneously evaluating the reconstructed images' accuracy and realness while also considering the statistical variance introduced by the probabilistic nature of multi-network learning. Moreover, the study reveals that this diverse neural ensemble approach can be applied to various, even different, PET scan conditions, as it demonstrates reduced variance and improved performance compared to a single-network approach, particularly when dealing with challenging low-dose images containing out-of-distribution noise realizations.

A revised expression of Centering Theory (CT) is proposed to provide a comprehensive explanation of how neural coreference resolvers function. The updated framework integrates three critical components: the identification of potential antecedents, the evaluation of their suitability, and the determination of their positional centrality. The positing of this framework is not merely descriptive, but also equips researchers with a structured approach to generate synthetic training data for neural coreference technology. The result is that existing datasets can be efficiently converted to conform to the standards of centering systems. To validate the centrality of our hypothesis, we developed a neural evaluator that aligns with this framework and discovered that the model's performance improves by approximately 5% when applied to the GCC and 3% when applied to Wikipedia-based coreference resolutions. The created synthetic data, along with the corresponding entity centrality labels, are made available to the public to facilitate further research.

The traditional method of determining the effective range of Wi-Fi access points involves measuring signal strength at specific, often inconvenient locations, such as the corners of a room. To address this issue, this study develops an innovative approach using machine learning algorithms to determine the effective range automatically. By utilizing real-world data collected from 802.11n protocol, we train and evaluate artificial neural networks to accurately predict range. The results show that these models can effectively classify range with high accuracy, outperforming traditional methods. Furthermore, this research highlights the suitability of using artificial intelligence in planning the deployment of wireless networks.

The beam fragmentation instabilities, exacerbated by the regenerative nature of energy recovery linacs (ERLs), can impair the accuracy of applications requiring high current density, such as high-resolution scattering experiments. Investigigating beam configuration impacts on instability thresholds, our study utilized the energy recovery linac (ERLTestBed) at Brookhaven National Laboratory. By varying beam configurations through magnetically decoupled bunch trains, our experimental results confirmed that higher form factor beams exhibit lower instability thresholds, confirming a prediction from theoretical models. The established threshold relationship was fitted with a power law, revealing that the instability threshold is proportional to the square root of the beam form factor. This discovery has practical significance for designing high-current applications in energy recovery linacs.

To enhance the $Q_g C_g$ impact factor to NNLL accuracy in the double Regge limit, we have developed an $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ correction to the vertex where two gluons with high momentum remain close in transverse space. This is achieved by calculating the $Q_g C_g$ contribution, where a high-momentum gluon and a small-transverse-size gluon dipole interact, in the context of $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. To handle the extensive phase space, we have adopted a helicity basis and expressed the impact factor using a set of scalar functions, with fourteen independent functions identified through analysis of the double-logarithmic region. We have derived analytic expressions for arguments of these functions using hypergeometric series, providing a more precise understanding of this complex theoretical space.

A novel analytical approach is applied to determine the behavior of molten polymer bristles with varying shapes, specifically for arbitrary profiles. According to a recent study, when a polymer brush is in its molten state, the segments near the base are densely packed and behave like a solid, whereas those in the outer area are loosely packed and behave like a liquid. We investigate the existence of a distinct exclusion region situated between these two areas. Through an adaptive mesh finite difference method, we determined the thickness of this exclusion region for polymers adhering to a substrate with a particular interaction pattern, known as the triblock copolymer brush model. Our analysis reveals that the exclusion region is consistently present and its size is influenced by several factors, including the length of the polymer segments, the density of the brush, and the interaction between the polymers and the substrate. Furthermore, we discovered that the exclusion region is consistently about two to three times the size of a single polymer segment, a characteristic that remains unchanged despite changes in the brush's overall properties.

A subset of vertices in a graph F is considered deterministic if, when combined with a function that maps the subset to a distinct sequence of coordinates in a Euclidean space, it helps pinpoint each vertex of the graph. The smallest possible size of such a subset is termed the shortened metric dimension. 

In this work, we provide a modified approach to find the shortened metric dimension of a graph and calculate this dimension for various types of graphs, including complete graphs, bipartite complete graphs, stars with deterministic leaves, and specific varieties of trees and ipogroups.

A notable achievement in astronomy astronomy in the last decade is all-sky map, which was created using machine learning techniques trained on all sky observations made over a short time period, primarily conducted by experiments like Fermi-LAT, which lasted around 11 years. These models have been shown to correct all-sky maps created using shorter observation periods, excelling in predicting the positions of moving objects, eclipsing objects, and objects with varying brightness, all of which were confirmed by follow-up observations. Full utilization of machine learning for all-sky maps is hindered due to the lack of detailed label information, which would enable precise identification of moving, eclipsing, and objects with varying brightness in all-sky maps created using machine learning techniques. Comprehensive annotation of moving objects, temporary objects, and objects with varying brightness in all-sky maps was examined, but full exploitation of machine learning for all-sky maps remains unclear due to the lack of detailed annotation.

A serial dictatorship mechanism is a method of reaching an efficient agreement among self-sufficient agents, who successively select goods or services from the remaining options. The timing of when each agent makes their choice can lead to varying outcomes, depending on whether the time frame is deterministic or stochastic. In a deterministic setting, the resulting agreement reflects a form of serial decision-making that embodies multiple utilitarian principles and, thus, can be seen as equivalent to the most favorable utilitarian outcome. However, in a stochastic setting, each possible arrangement becomes achievable with varying probabilities, and as such, can be characterized in terms of its probability distribution. We introduce and employ a probabilistic criterion for comparison, and with it, we are able to demonstrate that certain arrangements yield more favorable results than others in terms of this standard. We are also capable of formulating and using more intricate variations of this deterministic/ stochastic dichotomy, and with them, we can further enrich our understanding of when efficient agreements in a deterministic setting time it leads to results that can be regarded as inferior rather than enhancing those that are seen as desirable.

This research paper examines the features of minor planets with unusual light patterns in the Pan-STARRS1 Database. It highlights a crucial element - the absence of a significant brightness change - that distingu these objects and suggests they are likely singular bodies rather than binary systems. Although interesting, this characteristic does not substantially aid in exploring the mysteries of these objects' nature. The paper also introduces two additional, crucial parameters for analyzing these objects - the time it takes for any light pattern to repeat and the amount of time it takes for the binary system to complete one orbit. It scribes a formula that estimates the size of these objects based on a small light pattern's amplitude and the distance between them. Moreover, the paper discusses the challenges associated with detecting binary systems among the objects in the Pan-STARRS1 Database due to a variety of factors including orbital variations, rotating objects, reflections from objects with elliptical orbits, and objects covered in fast-moving loose surface debris.

Due to the rising significance of online networks in social interactions, researchers have explored the potential for leveraging network data to enhance the estimation and application of peer influence models. A key question arises as to whether a semi-parametric, linear regression approach can provide a reliable foundation for investigating peer influence within network settings. Our study delves into the implications of this approach, introducing a novel evaluation method known as network-aware cross-validation (n_cv). n_cv cross-fits both the dataset and the network structure, enabling a more accurate prediction of peer influence effects. We develop an consistency result, a mean squared error rate, and a recommendation for the optimal n_cv split strategy. A partially linear framework is then utilized to analyze peer influence in online networks, presenting empirical results from a peer influence dataset. These findings highlight the strength and positivity of peer influence, with n_cv demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional lock-split methods. Consequently, the presence of a network structure necessitates updated estimation techniques and cross-validation strategies, with n_cv cross-validation emerging as a effective and interpretable tool.

This study provides a enhanced understanding of the Leibniz Rule for the Riemann-Liouville variable-order integral and differential operator, filling a gap in fractional calculus theory. A total of 12 explicit examples are given to illustrate the practical applications of this improved theorem.

A collaborative study from University of Washington, Blizzard Entertainment, and UC Riverside explored how an AI could effectively communicate and guide players in a live Dungeons and Dragons game. The AI's role was narrowed down to a less powerful character, similar to a game master with limited capabilities. The research involved training the AI to understand players' communications using a large dataset, initially assuming a more powerful role, before testing its ability to guide players in real games with intentional discrepancies between its stated intentions and actual actions. The results revealed that the AI could successfully fulfill its guiding duties and engage in meaningful conversations with players, although it struggled to effectively influence their behavior in more intricate scenarios. The study provides an outline for advancing social guidance skills of less powerful entities.

A statistical investigation is conducted on four intricate knot types found in 32 simulated proteins under bending constraints as they transition from an unknotted to an unknotted state. Proteins are modeled using self-avoiding random walks and explore four distinct configurations: a free chain, one nestled within a tube, another tightly coiled within its own structure, and a final configuration with a loose end inserted into a closed loop. Our analysis reveals that the intricate knot types exhibit higher temperatures of formation for both knots and constituent parts that serve as seat and stem. Additionally, there is a direct correlation between the specific knot configuration and the average bending temperature of the proteins, indicating that more intricate knots result in higher temperatures. The study also reveals that the interaction between the free chain and the closed loop varies significantly across the different knot types and throughout the proteins' environments. Based on these findings, a selection criterion is established by averaging the temperature of formation for both the knot and a particular component, demonstrating that this method accurately replicates the results obtained from a more computationally intensive simulation model.

We define a new invariant, the symplectic mapping category group, for symplectic paths within specific classes of paths that connect points in symplectic manifolds, denoted as $(M, \omega)$. These categories help distinguish symplectic paths even when their starting and ending points coincide. In the context of $T^2$ blowups, we demonstrate that these invariants are meaningful and can be calculated, providing a measurable extension of the contact structure on the unit coadjoint orbit's boundary.

A theoretical extension of the Nambu-Goldstone theorem, known as the irregular Nambu-Goldstone theorem, is introduced in both relativistic and nonrelativistic quantum field contexts. This extension addresses the issues arising from a irregular singularity at the zero of the symmetry generator, resulting in an extra pole in the corresponding scalar particle's propagator at the same position as the spontaneous symmetry breaking mass. We provide several supporting equations from literature, particularly from literature regarding scalar QED with a complex Higgs field in the presence of a constant Abelian gauge field background. This constant field background leads to the generation of this irregular singularity, also observed in theories with global or local gauge symmetries and various scalar fields with different bosonic interactions. We discuss the physical consequences of this phenomenon, noting the presence of a new type of neutralscalar boson with a infinite dipole moment, and highlighting the need to classify this boson as a true Nambu-Goldstone particle.

Counterfactual phrases represent the distinction between how things are and how they could be, providing a valuable tool for humans to acquire knowledge. To meet the demands of various natural language inference tasks, it's essential to automatically generate these phrases. Current methods in this area, however, struggle to effectively capture the complex relationship between facts and their alternatives. To address this, an innovative NLP framework called DISCO has been developed, which isolates the complex relationship between facts and their counterfactuals into an intermediate representation called a seed. This allows for the generation of diverse counterfactual phrases through an iterative refinement process, incorporating an atom rewriter and a counterfactual evaluator. The results obtained from the DISCO framework significantly surpass those of strong baseline approaches in multiple natural language inference datasets, particularly in terms of R-F1 scores.

Epitaxial formation on opposite sides of graphene encrusting sapphire bases offers a route to produce high-purity Heusler compounds suitable for spintronic applications. The remote epitaxial technique enables precise control of chemical composition and crystalline structure. Yet, recent findings suggest that remote and vacuum epitaxy bridge with no evident gaps between them. This discovery necessitates updating the make-up of the precursor powder's equilibrium between pinhole and van der Waals epitaxy components. The made-up equation involves a layer component that epitaxially forms directly on the sapphire base. We discuss the equation's implications and design a system of heusler compounds to test the design through an in-depth study of MnPtSb on graphene/蓝宝石.
