To predict the long-term behavior of many-atom systems to even approximate true chaos levels remains a significant challenge in our field of research involving single atoms at a time. To precisely characterize true chaos within a single atom at a time, we must first grapple with the inherent limitations of wave function measurements, as they introduce statistical uncertainties that may potentially overwhelm the minuscule signatures of chaos. To effectively address this challenge, we are calling for the development of robust and scalable chaos prediction methods that can be directly applied to experimental settings. To demonstrate the potential applications, we successfully applied a simple and effective graph neural network approach to predict the chaos levels of an alkali atom's state at a single moment, exhibiting generalization capabilities. Our results reveal that even the subtle chaos signals can be effectively detected and that our model possesses strong predictive accuracy and transferability across different atomic species. Furthermore, we established an exact link between the chaos level and the predicted lifetime of a single-atom state.

Consider a set of $n$ given numbers, representing the individual parameters of interest within a population. I introduce a generalized likelihood function, employing independent and non-identically distributed normal distributions with known means and variances. This function enables the estimation of a target parameter, specifically the average of these individual parameters. This likelihood framework is utilized to estimate the mean in sampling scenarios, both with and without replacement.

Knowledge tracing is crucial in adaptive learning to customize learners' experiences by analyzing their history. There are numerous methods based on machine learning and deep learning to analyze knowledge tracing. However, developing and testing these methods requires a significant effort to retrieve, clean, and verify training data. This effort detracts from focusing on core algorithm development and testing. To address this issue, we introduce PyKT, a Python framework for efficiently evaluating deep learning-based knowledge tracing systems. PyKT provides cleaned datasets, includes code to reproduce published results, and facilitates comparing the performance of different methods using the same data. The framework is open-source and available on GitHub at https://github.com/yuxiaoxiao/pykt. We encourage researchers in the field of adaptive learning to utilize PyKT for advancing knowledge tracing algorithms.

Consider a vector field $E$ that is elliptic on an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$, with dimension less than $2m$. We will examine how this implies the elliptic operator $u \mapdu{E}^m u$ has a restricted image. This in turn leads to establishing the existence of a fundamental solution with optimal polynomial growth properties, as well as establishing $H^{-1}(L^p(\mathcal{M})) \equi \Hu{-1}\left(\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{E}^m)\cap\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{E}^m)\right+\mathcal{R}\left(\mathcal{J}\right)$, for a broad spectrum of values for $p$. Here $\mathcal{J}$ denotes a smoothing operator that is equivalent to $\mathcal{E}^m$. This equality will have applications to establishing the solvability of the Cauchy problem, specifically $\mathcal{E}^m u(t,x) = \du{t}v(t,x)$, along with the surjectivity of $u \mapdu{E}^mu$ for a variety of settings.

Our presentation will focus on the details of Alethe, an format dedicated to representing verified facts using universal logic, with support for sorted types and saturating arithmetic, as well as an expansion upon the work of Gratzl et al in 2017.



At the moment, obtaining reliable proofs with modern automated tools often requires conversion to specific tools' proprietary evidence formats. This format, however, facilitates the direct use of compiled tools without conversion, with all necessary tool-specific information clearly documented in the file format's specification.



The Alethe format also features efficiency-orientated design elements, including compact file sizes, use of GCode-like instructions for efficient parsing, an included standard library interface, and the ability to compact multiple provenances into a single file.



We will discuss the reasons behind the design choices made for the Alethe format as well as its potential applications, with examples including its utilization in major open-source projects involving formal verification.



The format's versatility is further illustrated with cases from the Crypto and Computer Science tracks of conferences including ACM CCS, FOSSACS, and USENIX Security, with references to related formats including Coq-Evide, Easy, Isabelle/UPF, and ProofWriter.

This paper explores the reasons behind the success of the tuned gradient method in federated learning scenarios. Although it has been widely adopted, there's theoretically unsupported evidence for its performance. By analyzing the synchronous aggregation process in ML systems, we examine the impact of data provided to model updates. In many cases, we discover that as long as updates are equally valuable during the aggregation process, previous concerns about data validity disappear. This finding enables us to conclude the practical utility of the tuned gradient method for SF-Prole applications. Moreover, it allows us to propose the buffer protocol, which involves utilizing arbitrary data buffers to achieve this. We compare the synchronous buffered approach to the unconstrained version and demonstrate their equivalence in terms of model performance. Consequently, it provides a strong foundation for the widespread use of the buffer protocol in real-world applications involving large-scale mobile data.

An interesting observation in ASR systems is their remarkable performance with non-standard pronunciations, despite being trained and assessed on clear, standard speech. This phenomenon suggests ASR systems' robustness to difficult, ambiguous sounds could be harnessed for transfer learning. Our research explores using a basic, "over-regularizer" based on ASR's uncertainty signals to facilitate transfer across speech qualities in spoken language tasks. Using parallel datasets with varying levels of clarity and complexity, our proposed method successfully enhances low-resource conditions when working with less high-fidelity recordings.

Autonomous robots are increasingly operating in dynamic environments, but traditional NavPix systems developed for static settings struggle when conditions change. This research presents a novel probabilistic model based on sparse Gaussian processes to detect and adapt to temporal variations in navigation skills. By making efficient use of computational resources, the model allows for real-time adaptation without requiring excessive training data. The proposed approach integrates a sensorimotor loop that automatically adjusts navigation policies for a fully autonomous surface vehicle. The paper outlines this system and provides a comparative analysis with a staple Reinforcement Learning alternative. Through a series of controlled experiments in simulated environments, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance.

We consider a static spherical body in General Relativity comprising two fluid layers and fluid interface with no thickness, demonstrating that under specific conditions it behaves as if it were a single-fluid body. We establish a rigorous mathematical framework for describing such configurations through first-order jump conditions at the interface, drawing inspiration from the principles of relativistic fluid dynamics. It becomes apparent that from a purely gravitational standpoint, the interface can be modeled using simpler second-order jump conditions. However, these conditions lack the capacity to represent bodies with non-uniform density distributions as 'celestial bodies'. We prove that any first-order condition can be equivalently transformed into various forms of 'celestial bodies', including those with constant density. As a consequence, any configuration consisting of two fluid layers separated by an interface can be regarded as a celestial body, consisting of an inner core and an outer shell with identical density. This equivalence also applies to configurations comprising multiple layers or clusters of cores encased in a common shell. Despite its name, this concept extends beyond astronomical contexts and can be applied to laboratory settings, for instance, to describe inertial confinement fusion targets consisting of a fuel shell, an opaque shell, and a dense core.

Most current methods for correcting grammatical errors rely on models trained with large amounts of data, which are highly dependent on the specific features of the target domain and don't effectively handle new, unseen domains. In contrast, our proposed approach, a novel meta-learning framework, focuses on achieving effectiveness with just a few examples, transferring knowledge from related source domains to target domains, without fine-tuning. We successfully apply this framework, Recen, to EFL error correction, demonstrating its ability to generalize across 14 unseen EFL related domains, outperforming state-of-the-art single-domain training and common transfer learning techniques. Our results highlight the potential of meta-learning to enhance cross-domain transfer for EFL error correction.

Resource allocation scenarios often involve widespread participation, where enough agents collectively determine the distribution of resources. When resources are not easily divisible, such as voting rights in a political decision-making process, it is crucial for our algorithms to identify equilibria that are fair and promote social good. Unfortunately, the literature mainly focuses on the existence of equilibria, with less emphasis on their fairness properties. In our proposed framework, we examine whether all pure Nash equilibria (PNEs) of a general game provide an equitable distribution of resources for all agents involved. We demonstrate that, for a wide range of game types including public goods provision, contribution games, and location games, the existence of at least one PNE is necessary and sufficient to ensure the uniform distribution of resources. Furthermore, the notion of uniformity can be expanded to include social welfare considerations.

A highly unusual star-forming galaxy, UGC 8839, was discovered to possess an extremely stable central disk through spectral analysis of its optical light, an endeavor that involved reconstructuring its two-dimensional velocity field.  This analysis revealed an exceptionally low level of disruption in the central disk, coupled with a surrounding spiral pattern, and led to the estimation of its total mass as being approximately 1.6 x 10^9 Msun.  Furthermore, a separate calculation based on its HII regions resulted in a bulge-to-total mass ratio of 0.1, which, although low, is notable for a low-redshift dwarf spiral galaxy.  Unusually, UGC 8839's central disk exhibits an extremely low level of scattering, an attribute typically associated with large, massive galaxies rather than low-surface brightness galaxies like itself. Given its specific characteristics, UGC 8839 cannot be effectively compared to a wide range of similar galaxies, and as such, it should be considered a distinct class in its own right.  In addition, an investigation into possible galaxy interaction history was conducted, yet no evidence of past or present galaxy interaction was found, making UGC 8839 an ideal candidate for further observational and theoretical study.

The equating of two-current formulations of the pion interacting nucleon current $J_N$ and pseudoscalar current $P$ has been demonstrated within a lattice QCD framework for $m_\pi$ values ranging from 216 MeV to 640 MeV, exceeding previous continuum extrapolations. This study also reanalyzed the proportionality coefficient $f$ from Ref.~{16} using lattice data for $m_\pi$ values ranging from 216 MeV to 640 MeV.

The youthful star, XX Cha, belongs to the Octans stellar constellation and is a member of the Ursa Major moving group, with an age ranging between 45 and 55 million years. Initially classified as a weak classical T Tauri star, a 2019 study re-categorized it as having an accretion disk. By monitoring the system's U band, H alpha, and Penn State emission lines for eight days at frequent intervals, researchers found that accretion rates fluctuate with a minimum and maximum value of 0.15 and 15 x 10^(-6) solar masses per year. These fluctuations could be caused internal factors like magnetic reconnection or impact clouds, rather than external obstructions. Notably, the lowest recorded accretion rates from previous studies match the extremes found in this study's data, suggesting that even active F stars can experience drops to such levels.

In human social interactions, individuals often focus on positive experiences rather than negative ones. This positive-based approach can lead to better cooperation. However, traditional methods that rely solely on positive feedback have limited success when it comes to multi-agent learning, especially among unfamiliar agents. We introduce LearnFromGoodPaths (L3GP), an innovative algorithm that enables multi-agent learning by leveraging states and actions associated with successful trajectories. Our method allows agents to prioritize experiences linked to successful outcomes, thereby facilitating more effective cooperation when working with previously unknown peers. Our approach has been shown to outperform existing control methods that allow agents to focus on positive experiences, as evidenced by improved results in both coordinated tasks and games requiring cooperation.

We investigated the use of 2D MV images for conformal radiotherapy treatment planning and image transfer. To enhance conformal capabilities, we developed a novel approach to bridge the gap between 2D MV images and treatment plans, employing a convolutional neural network (CNN) in both 3D and 2+3D settings. The study involved 43 MV images and utilized a CNN with four max-pooling layers and four dense layers. Our results showed high correlation between predicted and actual values, with SPCCPs exceeding 0.9 in most cases and accurate spatial displacement estimation, positioning, and orientation, demonstrating the potential of using 2D MV images for accurate image transfer and 3D MV image synthesis.

The single-particle scenario in guidance bias bias experiments is often overlooked, despite being genetically nonlocal. A purely local single-particle guidance bias scenario is demonstrated and analyzed. It's established that single-particle entanglement is necessary to generate guidance bias bias. A simple model is explored that displays single-particle entanglement, leading to a a nonlocal origin for a a single-particle guidance bias.

The burgeoning intricacy of vehicle-based learning systems creates an impending threat of sensitive data data breaches and monopolistic control, prompting the necessity for an innovative approach to share knowledge while safeguarding privacy and preventing data monopolies. A federated learning framework integrated with blockchain technology presents a prospective solution, though comprehensive research on this subject remains absent. This paper conducts in-depth analyses of vital FL applications within the Internet of Vehicles, elucidating the limitations of existing vehicle-based learning systems and the potential solutions offered by a federated environment. This research can direct future developments in vehicle-based learning and furnish practical guidance for implementing a federated learning framework in this domain. Moreover, this paper categorizes critical challenges and potential avenues for advancement in a FLEI framework, including the selection of an appropriate blockchain framework, consensus mechanisms, smart contracts for data verification, cryptographic protocols for privacy preservation, and novel consensus mechanisms that incorporate machine learning to enhance system efficiency.

V392 Persei, a novel star, has experienced two major explosions in a short period. The first occurred in 2010, with its spectrum characteristic of a under-luminous nova. Following this, observations with the VLA in 2010 and 2011 revealed the presence of a circumstellar disk. V392 Persei's second explosion, however, was far more intense and was accompanied by a series of high-energy events, including an X-ray burst and diffuse emission detected by Fermi-LAT, marking it as a hybrid nova. As a hybrid, its total energy output exceeded that of all other novae. V392 Persei's light curves, whether observed visually or in the X-ray spectrum, showed an intricate pattern resembling that of the 2010 explosion but with distinct differences. The energy source behind the X-rays switched from thermal gas in the 2010 explosion to a hot gas flow in the 2014 event. V392 Persei's high energy events were facilitated by a massive ejection of mass, even though the star was predicted to be old. The circumstances of these explosions, combined with its vibrant appearance, have made V392 Persei an intriguing subject of study.

A mobile device feedback mechanism has been proposed that leverages K-means algorithms to reduce memory usage. This approach entails the network providing a set of reference signals, known as RSUs, which the user equipment (UE) stores in its memory. These RSUs are then processed on the UE to create a codebook, with precomputed parameters facilitating efficient generation using minimal memory. A novel, compact encoding scheme has also be developed to enable the codebook and relevant parameters to be transmitted to the base station through limited feedback channels. Simulation results demonstrate that this technique yields significant throughputs when compared to conventional codebooks.

A key characteristic of homogeneous space differs from the principles of quantum holography. When a system reaches a steady nonequilibrium state, it can lead to current instabilities that cause the buildup of electric fields, which in turn can result in a sudden shift from a delocalized to a localized state, a phenomenon observed in experiments. Using a holographic approach, this study investigates the 3D Hofstadter model, a relativistic variant of the Hall effect, in its strong regime with multiple flavors in the presence of a strong perpendicular magnetic field and a local periodic potential. Findings suggest that a delicate interplay between the strength of this potential and the magnetic field strength can lead to the emergence of a robust transverse electric dipole in a region where surface charges accumulate on both the upper and lower edges of the system's energy spectrum. Moreover, this model also exhibits reflections of the photon drag effect, the generation of harmonic currents in response to an alternating magnetic field, and a form of the Hall effect in response to an alternating electric field. Furthermore, a robust edge-state quantum Hall effect has been discovered in a nonequilibrium setting under an alternating magnetic field.

For an B-type star situated in front of the supermassive black hole at the center of our galaxy, known as S2, calculations indicate that through accretion, the black hole could have significantly grown in mass over the past 10 billion years. However, observations show the mass has increased by less than one percent during this time. A star orbiting this black hole should have contributed to its growth by accreting approximately 2.5 solar masses. Given the lack of evidence for high-density gas near the black hole, it's likely that radiative forces caused some form of mass loss. In order to reconcile both mass gain and loss, the radiative forces between the gas and the black hole must be in a quasi-equilibrium over extended periods, allowing for limited net accretion. From this constraint, an upper limit can be set on the speed at which the black hole can grow by 0.1 percent per year. This limit also suggests that the black hole is surrounded by a thin ring of gas, no wider than 100 astronomical units.

The initial stars that inhabited globular clusters billions of years ago, particularly in nuclear star clusters at their centers, could have left behind observable remnants. We focus on three possible scenarios where these remaining stars might produce detectable gravitational waves. First, the collision and merging of massive stars in close encounters, and second, the interactions between massive stars and black holes, can occur as they orbit each other. A less obvious situation, however, arises when a binary star system enters the cluster, and its components trade partners through close encounters. If one of these interactions results in a massive star swapping with an intermediate-mass black hole, the resulting merger could produce detectable gravitational waves from the subsequent ringdown stage. We estimate the frequency of these events, focusing on well-known globular clusters as representatives. Our calculations suggest that collisions and mergers of massive stars and black holes, and even binary encounters, may leave behind populations of stellar black holes and intermediate-mass black holes in these clusters. Unfortunately, however, even with sensitive detectors like LISA, finding evidence of these hidden populations would be challenging.

Orthonormal frequency-domain spreading combined with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing offers an effective solution for securing wireless data transmissions and overcoming multi-path interference in OFDMA systems. However, this approach, exemplified by discrete Fourier transform encryption, consumes excessive transmission resources and is inefficient when relay nodes are used. This project proposes and analyzes an alternative encryption method, circular encryption, adapted for wireless systems with external relay nodes, focusing on additive white Gaussian noise relaying. By optimizing transmission power allocation and encryption keys, it aims to maximize transmission rates and minimize encryption overhead, considering various scenarios such as single and multiple user cases with single or multiple frequency bands. To achieve these goals, both relay selection and optimization algorithms are employed, comparing various encryption patterns and overhead levels in terms of system performance. Numerical results highlight key insights into system behavior and highlights the advantages of the proposed circular encryption scheme.

Agents that can navigate real-world tasks are significantly hindered by their slow processing times. In the TextWorld environment, which simulates text-based games, these agents struggle to keep up. To overcome this limitation, we introduce TextWorldExpress, an advanced processor based on TextWorld that can move at one million moves per second. By utilizing TextWorldExpress, state-of-the-art agents achieving performance levels comparable to human experts on complex tasks become feasible. When applied to the TextWorld puzzle platform, TextWorldExpress-enabled agents exhibit successful results.

A comparative study of neural network algorithms and hardware implementations has led to novel energy-efficient approaches in video recognition. This study presents both hardware and algorithmic innovations for sequence data processing. An analysis of deep learning structures reveals that Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are versatile and can mimic various other algorithms, albeit with varying levels of accuracy and temporal efficiency. This paper utilizes LMMS as a case study to showcase feasible methods for network optimization, including the application of hierarchical tensor formats to reduce the amount of computational effort and energy required. A system integrating a multi-level tensor network with corresponding hardware components has been developed to showcase the principles underlying such an approach, including optimized algorithms, reduced memory usage, and more efficient data management. Experimental results highlight the benefits of this method over conventional approaches, demonstrating up to 3.35 times greater efficiency in terms of execution time, along with significant improvements in memory consumption and storage.

In the study of local rings, we investigate the compact Hilbert polynomial as a tool to detect F-singularities. We demonstrate that a non-zero parameter ideal in a local ring generates a specific compact Hilbert polynomial if and only_modules generated by that ideal are F-separable. Additionally, we establish an condition where a local ring is F-rational based on the compact Hilbert polynomial being zero for some power of the assumption module. We also provide a equivalent characterization of F-pure rings using the compact Hilbert polynomial. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between compact Hilbert functions and torsion modules generated by the assumption module in the context of F-singularities.

The research community and practical industries are investing heavily in developing and refining agent-based models to tackle intricate issues. In order to improve the efficiency of auxiliary services trading within data centers, an agent-based approach has been implemented. The data center's heat management constraints, purchasing option prices and market engagement factors were incorporated into the model. Key elements such as prices, engagement levels and technical limits were examined through extensive experiments to assess how they influenced the results. Furthermore, these findings were compared to those obtained from a conventional optimization approach. It was discovered that several engagement elements could significantly impact the efficiency of auxiliary services trading within data centers, with some producing contrary effects. Additionally, the research highlights the importance of integrating data center market engagements in the development of policy guidelines related to auxiliary services trading. Finally, the research underscores the versatility of using agent-based models to investigate and resolve complex issues involving multiple factors that cannot be adequately addressed through conventional modeling techniques.

Let P_q(K) signify the set of all prime numbers less than or equal to q within the integers P, where q belongs to K. Let's consider two finite collections of prime numbers, P_{p_1} and P_{p_2}, where p_1 and p_2 are distinct prime numbers. A consequence of the Chinese Remainder Theorem is that for any given set of residues a(x) modulo p_1 and b(x) modulo p_2, where both are relatively prime to their respective moduli, we can find a prime number p within P_{p_1} and p_{p_2} such that p is congruent to a(p) (mod p_1) and b(p) (mod p_{p_2}). This can be expressed as p is congruent to c(p) (mod M), where M is the product of p_1 and p_{p_2}, and c(x) is the result of combining the two modular systems. By repeatedly applying this process, we can establish that for any number of collections of prime numbers and corresponding moduli, we can also find a prime number that is congruent to a specific residue modulo the product of all the moduli.

Analysis of atmospheric features in front of the Saturn northern polar vortex reveals an intriguing hexagonal shape that emerged over a two-week period during June 2020. This discovery is unlike previous observations, where gradual changes over months or years were typically observed. A similar, though less distinct, hexagonal pattern was found in the 1990s by the VIMS instrument on the Hubble Space Telescope. The causes behind this phenomenon remain unknown, but several theoretical models have been proposed. These models suggest either wind Enstrophy conservation or radiative-convective processes could be driving the formation of these hexagons. An investigation into the polar region's temperature patterns did not provide substantial evidence to support the radiative-convective model's predictions, which propose that warm winds enclose a cold core.

We consider a Schrödinger equation with an attractive, point-wise confining potential within a domain bounded by a convex hull in a two-dimensional space. It is shown that the equation will undergo a blow-up phenomenon for all initial conditions with a fixed L2 norm. However, when the equation is modified to have an intense nonlinearity, there is no explosion time solution for initial conditions with zero phase. Instead, the solution grows without bound at an infinite rate, following a predictable inverse time function. All peak points of the solution develop simultaneously, and the individual points grow infinitely large.

This paper explores the concept of local uniform abbreviations (LUA) for algebraic varieties in the context of positive characteristic, extending a previously developed, characteristic-zero, semi-parametric framework. Given a set of local presentations for a variety V defined over a non-negative characteristic field, we establish sufficient conditions, specific to each characteristic, that ensure V maintains consistency across all characteristics. Notably, we demonstrate that when the presented variety has a complexity exceeding 3, there exists an alternative, simpler description with lower complexity. Furthermore, we examine the relationship between LUA and other abbreviation methods, including Grobner bases, and provide examples to highlight the distinctions between these approaches.

In the field of combinatorial sequences, a new operation called "polarization" is introduced, which serves as an analog to the "difference" operation introduced by Karu. This operator preserves the property of being positively polarized and has additional properties such as reducing the degree of a collection by one, mirroring how the difference degree behaves. When applied twice, it mimics the fundamental difference operator's effect. When combined with other operations like cyclic sums, it can result in either the zero collection or a constant multiple of a basic collection. This is similar to a key property of the fundamental difference operator in combinatorial analysis. Ultimately, both the difference and polarization operators share the same underlying purpose, which can be understood through their effect on the combinatorial graphs associated with the collections they operate on.
This article explores the technical issues related to the measurement of orbital integrits standardizations of measures.

Utilizing synchrotron radiation, we investigated the capabilities of X-ray absorption and resonant x-ray scattering to detect and characterize the pre-transitional phases of materials. While x-ray absorption spectra are well-established in identifying local atomic configurations, we explored how resonant x-ray scattering signals can be interpreted to detect long-range order. Focusing on La$_{2-x}$Sr$_{x}$CuO$_4$ as a model system, we analyzed a range of doping levels near $x=0.05$ to confront existing theoretical interpretations. By combining existing and new experimental data, we developed a unified model to better understand this region of the phase diagram. Furthermore, we highlight the significance of using resonant x-ray scattering to detect the coexistence of different phase domains within materials.

This study uses a mixed-complementary finite element approach to single-phase Darcy flow in fractured and homogeneous media.
We incorporate a "jump condition" into the model that accounts for flow across fracture interfaces based on the difference in hydraulic head across the fractures.
It is noted that this problem generally lacks a unique solution when the fractures contain closed loops.
To address this, a orientation are normal vector for each fracture is defined.
This technique yields a fully mixed method equivalent to a discrete weak formulation with pressure test functions in both the main body and the fractures.
This approach eliminates the need for a separate grid near the fractures, leading to significant computational benefits.
Furthermore, it guarantees a conservative numerical solution and provides a valid local pressure approximation even in closed-loop fractures with no fluid flow.
Numerical examples are provided to validate the technique's reliability, along with convergence theorems for $H(\text{div})$- and $L^2$-errors.

The Bayes factor stands out as a prominent hypothesis testing method, offering several benefits over other approaches. Despite these advantages, practical adoption of Bayes factors in iterative settings is hindered by a few key challenges: the high computational costs of estimating Bayes factors through Monte Carlo methods, difficulties in accurately estimating Bayes factors via analytical methods, and the need to预先define, in contrast to the flexibility of likelihood ratios to adjust after data collection. This paper delves into the issues surrounding the efficient utilization of Bayes factors in an iterative context and explores various robust strategies for estimation and management. We also present and analyze multiple statistical approaches, including the adaptive sampling strategy originally developed by Freedman (1990) for determining when to stop the iteration process, utilizing concepts such as log-loss, information gain, and Bayes factors.

In daily conversations, certain words such as "because," "however," and "although" are used to express causal connections, contrasts, and concessions, which can significantly influence how we process and make sense of the information presented. Indicators of these logical relationships are known as discourse markers or indicators, which have long fascinated linguists but received relatively less attention in the field of natural language processing, likely due to the lack of high-quality training data. This study introduces a novel examination of English discourse indicators, encompassing their capacity to express different types of relationships, as well as characteristics that may affect their performance. Furthermore, a substantial corpus consisting of 55,000 instances is created, leveraging open-source resources, and a set of research questions is explored through statistical analysis, including the development of a few targeted machine learning models.

From the perspective of convex optimization, we offer a groundbreaking theory on the nonconvex matrix decomposability. This idea paves the way for a new approach to nonconvex matrix problems by introducing a concept known as "geodesic convexity." Specifically, we establish the nonconvex matrix decomposability for a broad class of loss functions, demonstrating that within a particular domain, a specific norm's subset is both convex and has a property where all geodesics are convex. From this property, various outcomes can be deduced, including a proof of the global effectiveness of local optimization methods for low-rank matrix problems on a nonconvex landscape, which is smooth and uniformly star-convex from the origin. Moreover, our origin-centered geodesic convexity framework has a broader scope than recent approaches, providing a unified analysis for low-rank matrix problems, including those involving the L1 norm, and even allowing for the investigation of convexity in other underexplored norm spaces.

A graph is considered edge-tinted if its edges can be divided into two parts such that each part forms a matching. For many types of graphs, being bipartite is an equivalent condition to being edge-tinted, but this rule does not hold for all cubic bipartite graphs. In response to an open question posed by Awamleh and MacGillivray, we provide a specific example of a bipartite cubic graph that is not edge-tinted, thus demonstrating that even when a graph is bipartite, it does not necessarily have to be edge-tinted.

We investigated the effectiveness of coevolutionary genetic algorithms in reaching a Nash equilibrium for a symmetrical Cournot game with step-by-step player interactions. Although these algorithms generally resulted in outcomes close to the theoretical Nash equilibrium, we found instances where they led to stable strategies that maximised payoffs given the other player's typical approach, often far from the optimal payoff given a random opponent. Notably, when players played repeatedly in a partner-based scenario, these strategies attracted and locked into populations. Furthermore, when one player could observe the other before gameplay, the observing player could consistently outperform both the Nash equilibrium and the mutual matching strategies.

For any given weighted directed graph, we examine the ideal generated by the edges of the graph and determine under what conditions this ideal shares the same algebraic properties as its directed, undirected counterpart. Specifically, we establish criteria for the ideal to have a unique resolution pattern (linear resolution) and to satisfy the decomposition property, when both concepts are transferred to the weighted directed setting. Additionally, we explore the ideal's behavior when the graph's structure forms a specific type of tree-like orientation and when it represents a fully connected, weighted undirected graph in either direction. These explorations are supported by the development of key lemmata that support our main conclusions.

The success of deep learning systems depends on their accuracy and resistance to adversarial attacks. Neural networks are often deployed on embedded devices due to their power efficiency, but hardware faults in these devices can affect the performance and safety of machine learning models. A previous study demonstrated that for certain applications, neural networks can be made resilient to hardware errors by adjusting the thresholds of neural activations without significantly increasing computational costs. In order to validate these findings, a new open-source toolkit called ConvNetGuard was developed to detect and prevent harmful errors by modifying the resilience of a neural network. ConvNetGuard includes a novel algorithm that determines the optimal threshold settings for each layer of the network. The development of ConvNetGuard facilitates the integration of hardware resilience into neural networks for classified security research. Each layer of the network is protected by setting upper and lower limits on the values of its activations, which can be efficiently managed with minimal computational overhead. The results obtained using ConvNetGuard demonstrate that adjusting the resilience of each layer individually leads to improved overall resistance to adversarial examples and provides a realistic approach to ensuring the reliability of neural networks on embedded devices.

A family of Jordanian twists is established, extending and refining the findings of Ref.4 with a specific parameter set, and it is shown to have a direct correspondence with the modified Jordanian quantum Tatalibeh algebras through a 1-cocycle relationship, after applying a 1-cohomology equivalence transformation.

If a set of words produces the same level of semantic information across multiple languages, it equates to a universal vocabulary. Despite numerous studies on word representation, creating a cluster-consistent set across different languages remains a complex task. We propose a novel, unsupervised framework called the Multi-lingual Shared Semantic Space (MSSS) that generates a common set of word clusters across at least two languages without relying on external knowledge. This is achieved by ensuring that words which belong to similar clusters are grouped together and that the structure of our framework mirrors the inherent organization of word clusters in each language. When evaluated using a variety of metrics, including mutual information, the MSSS framework demonstrates superior performance in comparing word representation methods and generating a shared semantic space for a English-Spanish language pair.

This research analyzes identified particle production in Xe-Xe collisions at 5.44 TeV, focusing on key observables such as transverse momentum distributions, particle ratios, and collective flow for pions, kaons, (anti-)protons, and $\phi$ mesons. 
Our study builds upon similar analyses from Au-Au and Pb-Pb collisions, and relies on theoretical models including thermodynamic statistics, coherent sources, and miniathermal gas. 
Moreover, comparisons with the AMPT and URQMD simulations, as well as data from various collision types, highlight the significant role of collective behavior even at preliminary stages. 
However, to fully understand these observations, a comprehensive analysis of secondary particle production within the thermodynamic framework is essential, and thus calls for rigorous calculations within advanced simulations like the Boltzmann Transport Equation, MB, and hadron resonance gas models, and from an experimental perspective, in heavy ion collisions at intermediate energies.

In November 2019, Chile experienced widespread unrest fueled by nearly three weeks of extensive nationwide demonstrations and destructive riots. This project develops an agent-based model to replicate and analyze these riots' spread across various Chilean neighborhoods. The incorporation of map-based data enables the modeling of simultaneous riots in different areas of the country. The model replicates observed rioting patterns and yields insights into their epidemiological-like dynamics. Furthermore, it explores potential policy interventions aimed at disrupting transmission networks. Notably, we discover that the transmission rules' parameters do not universally apply to all regions of the country.

This research provides an expanded subset of previous work, specifically dealing the inclusion of extended regular expressions within the Kozen-Varadarajan framework. We utilize a closure operation to establish that all inequalities involving these expressions can be reduced to a finite set of automata-based inclusion checks. A key finding is that regular expression equality is decidable when "reverse" and star operations are considered. The proof of this property relies on converting the reverse of a given regular expression into a standard form, thereby allowing closure operations to preserve equality and enabling the application of Northcutt's improvement to Overmars' algorithm for pairwise intersection computation. As a result, the decision problem for reverse regular expression equality is solvable.

A notable challenge in mobile visual navigation is effectively utilizing external memory to guide navigation based on a given instruction and visual input. Existing real-time vision-and-inertial navigation systems fall short in this task, primarily due to their reliance on inertial measurement units, their failure to utilize deep visual features, and their inadequate fusion of visual and inertial data. In contrast, our approach, EMA-VIO, addresses these limitations by integrating deeply learned visual features, efficiently navigating with an inertial-based method, and ensuring robust performance through a uniquely designed fusion of visual and inertial information, allowing our system to selectively focus on relevant parts of the memory and accurately track targets in dynamic scenes. Our results show that our approach, EMA-VIO, outperforms the state-of-the-art in video navigation by significantly improving navigation accuracy and minimizing the impact of the initial position on performance.

Quantum states with elevated band gaps typically display robustness against disturbances and expansive proximity effects. We introduce a novel type of elevated Weyl semimetal that features square-root elevated quadratic points in place of traditional Weyl points, demonstrating the fundamental characteristics of elevated quantum states, with the ability to enclose elevated quantum Hall effect states and Hall drift channels through the formation of Landau levels within a 3D space. Additionally, we introduce the concept of a hybrid elevated quantum Hall effect that arises from the interaction between elevated Weyl points and higher-order nodal lines, as well as elevated Fermi arc states that appear at the surface of the material.

This study investigates the quasi-reversibility technique in solving a problem where additional information, such as magnetic or electric field components, is improperly provided. The issue at hand involves finding a source term in the time-dependent Maxwell's equations within a spatial domain, given incomplete and noisy data representing the time evolution of the system. We establish the stability of solutions when boundary conditions are imposed on a spatial domain without change and introduce a discrete approach using finite elements to both spatial and temporal dimensions. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through several test cases.

When combining knowledge from various sources, it's crucial to consider the quality and reliability of each source. A new approach called Federated Discriminative Aggregation (FedDA) integrates knowledge from multiple experts who share information in a decentralized manner, without directly exchanging data. In FedDA, each expert maintains a set of neural network parameters and updates them based on new knowledge, with the aggregation performed in two distinct phases: locally, each expert refines the network, and then a learning rate is adjusted, with the updated parameters shared and aggregated. The final integrated knowledge is held in a centralized location. FedDA involves two key components: individual knowledge enhancement and FedAvg-based aggregation. The method is designed to handle situations where experts have different sets of data, and it has been applied to both multi-task and knowledge fusion scenarios. Experimental results show that FedDA outperforms existing consolidated knowledge approaches.

We analyze the rank growth of elliptic curves within two specific quartic field families, those with Galois groups $S_4$ and $A_4$, by studying a specific quartic polynomial and its quadratic subfield. Notably, the average rank of curves within both $S_4$ and $A_4$ quartic fields matches that of their underlying quadratic field. This result is supported by numerical data and theoretical prediction, derived from an adapted Largin-Duquesne formula, which accounts for solvability of certain Diophantine equations for both Galois groups.

In the study of quantum thermodynamics within the holographic framework, a novel expression for the quantum extensibility bound, tailored to local entropy loss, is established and denoted as $\alpha_{\mathrm{QE}}\geq 3c/ \hbar\sqrt{G_N}$. By analyzing the relationship between the entropy loss and the entanglement expansion across null-separated boundaries, this expression is shown to be crucial in determining the maximum expansion rate of entanglement, especially for null directions where the boosted null energy condition fails to provide a meaningful constraint. A specific application to the past horizon complement's expansion rate reveals that the quantum extensibility bound offers the most restrictive constraint, superseding both the boosted and ordinary null energy conditions. Furthermore, an inverse result is proven, stating that the quantum extensibility bound can be derived from the past horizon complement's past inequality. In a second application, the past horizon complement's average energy density is expressed, which is absent in classical theories and considered a new term in the quantum correction to the null Cosmological First Law.

A new type of time scale, called a discriminability duration, is introduced to identify the minimum time required for a quantum system to transition between two distinguishable states. In a mathematical framework, the discriminability distance is represented as a metric and related to the Fubini-Study distance. In the context of the Bloch sphere, a family of discriminability durations is parameterized by an asymmetry index, which influences the quantum velocity bounds. These bounds are characterized by three distinct regimes with different bounds for radial, tangential, and combined motions. Notably, in the BOB (Bohmic) representation, these durations are related to both tangential and radial velocities. Furthermore, a general inequality is established, stating that the longest discriminability duration varies monotonically with an asymmetry index. In addition, a mean theorem is introduced to facilitate a concise proof of this inequality using an explicit expression for the duration's curvature.

Superconducting quantum circuits are advancing rapidly, yet there are significant challenges related to coherence. To progress in this field, it is crucial to develop near-field terahertz imaging techniques that can operate at the frequency scale. This paper presents the design, frequency range extension, and application of a terahertz near-field scanning microscope specialized for coplanar microwave resonators. By extending the instrumentation's frequency range to 0.7 THz through careful optimization and utilizing a glider antenna with enhanced sensitivity, notable results were achieved. The microscope successfully mapped the spatial distribution of the electric and magnetic fields, demonstrated terahertz spectroscopy with high frequency precision, and exhibited a terahertz imaging resolution of 20 x 20 nm^2 with a 20 nm sample scanning step.

This work examines the long-duration evolution of planetary atmospheres, with a focus on Venus, by exploring theoretical models. Various approaches are compared and contrasted to discuss the diverse ways in which the atmosphere may change over time. An overview is provided regarding the analysis of the impact of magnetic fields, in both the upper and lower atmospheres, on the overall evolution. Ultimately, several "feedback loops" are considered that may influence the modification of the atmosphere.

Point processes that rely on pairwise interactions are widely seen as effective
tools for describing intricate patterns in extensive data sets of observed
events. The Bayesian approach to parameter estimation in these models often faces
constraints due to the potential for self-excitation to cause a high risk of
events overflowing. In this paper, we introduce the Bayesian analysis of a
nonlinear Hawkes model with an semi-andally parametric self-excitation function
that allows for the assessment of model parameters in a fully Bayesian framework.
This involves showing how to derive the posterior distribution without using
Monte Carlo methods for sequential sampling. We also discuss the use of a
nonlinear Hawkes model in the context of earthquake data sets and provide an
example with real-world data to support our findings.

Plasma-based systems have gained significant attention as powerful tools for generating highly polarized laser pulses and a range of physics phenomena. Despite extensive research, the optimal method for achieving strong laser pulse and subsequent particle generation remains debated. This study demonstrates that a circularly polarized laser pulse with multiple petawatt power levels can be produced for the first time in a straight section of plasma, and circular polarization yields higher electron emission and radiation generation compared to linear polarization. It is shown that an applied magnetic field can be used to control the degree of circular or linear conversion, and there is an anomalous increase in radiation production at specific magnetic field strengths. Furthermore, high-power circular polarization can be achieved over a wide range of plasma conditions and is robust against small deviations, and a circularly polarized drive pulse results in an asymmetrical acceleration pattern that enhances the probability of photon emission.

A thorough investigation into the electric dipole of the tau lepton is being undertaken, with an in-depth analysis of recent experimental data and theoretical constraints on possible values for its electric dipole moment and chromoelectric dipole moment. Notable current limits on these values are as follows: $|d_\tau| < 8.4 \times 10^{-17}~e~\mathrm{cm}$ (95% confidence level), originating from searches for lepton-flavour violating processes in experiments at LEP; and $|d_\tau| < 4.04 \times 10^{-19}~e~\mathrm{cm}$ (95% confidence level), from experiments at B-factories. Similarly, bounds on the chromoelectric dipole moment of the tau are as tight as $|d_\tau^c| < 2.64 \times 10^{-16}~e~\mathrm{cm}$ (95% confidence level). From the perspective of physics beyond the Standard Model, the electric dipole of the tau lepton is sensitively linked to new sources of CP-violation. In certain scenarios, such as in two-Higgs-doublet models, observable effects would emerge from this phenomenon.

For several decoding scenarios involving rank errors with a symmetry constraint, we establish a general approach to achieving efficient computation. This is accomplished by leveraging orthogonal transformation matrices that preserve the integrity of instances within their own group, thus enabling the size of a problem to be reduced and its decoding to be resolved with a complexity of O(n log n) in time and n log n to memory, where n represents the combined number of rows and columns in a data matrix. This is a significant improvement over existing methods, which require higher computational resources. Furthermore, our proposed solution includes a efficient way to verify the correctness of decoded instances.

In the context of a unitary conformal field theory on two-dimensional space-time, known as CFT$_2$, there is a well-established result stating that the set of primary operators in the operator product expansion (OPE) of two stress-energy tensors forms a complete set. This completeness ensures that the set of conformal blocks derived from this OPE spans the space of solutions to the Ward identities associated with Virasoro symmetry. However, recent findings challenge this result by demonstrating instances where the set of primary operators fails to account for the entire spectrum of conformal blocks in certain three-dimensional gravitating quantum field theories, described as W$_{1+\infty}$-invariant in AdS$_3$. This discrepancy also implies limitations in the applicability of the Fefferman-Graham expansion to a broad category of unitary CFT$_2$ theories, specifically those residing in the intermediate conformal window, characterized by primary operators lying within a specific range of conformal dimensions and spins. Moreover, it leads to conclusions about the structure of the OPE coefficients of the double-trace operators in these theories.

In 1992, Gelfand and MacPherson developed a foundational enumerative approach to defining and understanding topological invariants, particularly the Pontrjagin classes. Although their method proved effective, key aspects of their initial ideas remained unexplored for nearly two decades. This note fills that knowledge gap by discussing further enumerative aspects of Gelfand and MacPherson's work, specifically relating their findings to a classical problem posed by Steenrod and providing an original geometric interpretation of their key identity connecting the Pontrjagin classes to Euler classes.

We have obtained high-cadence photometric and spectroscopic data for Sn 2020jfo, initially classified as a Type II spectrum but later confirmed as a supernova with a disk-like structure. Sn 2020jfo belonged to the normal variety of core-collapse supernovae with extended hydrogen features. A notable examination focused on its transition from the free-expansion stage to the optical depth-stable stage, during which the classification as a Type II was made. Sn 2020jfo exhibited a short, flat period in its light curve, although this feature was not prominently visible in all optical brightness measurements. A analysis of the supernova's spectrum during the initial stages revealed an estimated mass of its hydrogen envelope to be between 0.27 and 0.34 solar masses. Sn 2020jfo's characteristics aligned with other astronomical events exhibiting a faint or absent optical depth-stable period, often grouped together as a subtype of Type II supernovae with extended hydrogen features. However, unlike some of these events, Sn 2020jfo lacked a subsequent peak in its light curve associated with the breakdown of hydrogen line confusion.

To greatly reduce the number of detectors required in wide-field X-ray systems, a new design called a lobster-eye array may allow for effective multiplexing. This paper explores the theoretical aspects of such a system and highlights its potential use in wide-field X-ray instruments. By employing a lobster-eye array, the satellite X-MOM, described in an accompanying paper, could potentially monitor a large area of sky around 100 times more effectively than its predecessor, the satellite MEGACO-2. X-MOM is planned to be built in the near future.

We explore a "stage set" interpretation of uniform and partial uniform ellipticity in the uniform structureless equation: $u_t+\Delta_p u+f(\Delta_{p}u)=g(u,\nabla_{p}u,x)$. Here, we examine how the condition of uniform ellipticity can be relaxed without causing issues with well-posedness. Despite the $f$ function lacking continuity, we establish the existence of a solution to this $p$-Dirichlet problem when $p$ is greater than $2$. Moreover, for values of $p$ between $2$ and $2+\delta$, we prove that the solution $u$ possesses a non-zero measure.

A novel theoretical concept, the cosmic speed field (CSF), was introduced by a few researchers recently. Deep learning methods were employed to examine the connection between CSF and the properties of dark matter halos, with a focus on their masses. It was discovered through statistical analysis using machine learning that dark matter halos with masses differing by up to 11 orders of magnitude exhibit nearly the same average speeds, with a standard deviation of about three times their mass. Furthermore, using simulated N-body data, a precise relationship was established between the densities of these halos and their associated speeds, with a standard deviation of only 20 percent. This led to a probabilistic framework for describing the distribution of dark matter halos based on their masses, spins, and the cosmic speed field.

We have formulated a general theory of relativity model including rotation to analyze rotating black hole spacetimes. This framework consists of two main components: an asymmetric stress-energy tensor describing accretion or outflows in the outer regions, and a rotating fluid in the inner regions that connects to the outer regions through specific conditions. Based on this framework, we have developed equations of motion, continuity, and boundary conditions in a stationary and axially symmetric context. These equations can be expressed in terms of conserved quantities, enabling efficient integration even with slow convergence methods. We have tested this method in two common scenarios: the growth of black holes through accretion and the outflows from black holes. Additionally, we have explored the connection between our formulation and other approaches within this framework.

The emergence of advanced document processing technologies has also brought an issue of high labeling expenses due to the complex, visually abundant nature of modern documents. This paper introduces several strategies to simplify the labeling process for a state-of-the-art document extraction framework, CORD, by introducing simplified annotation levels and leveraging a pre-existing visual element database. This approach streamlines the creation of a comprehensive dataset for an under-explored category of documents. When applied to a new dataset, FIN documents, our method results in a approach that is 10 times faster and 81 times less expensive than a conventional labeling approach. When combined with a strategic element selection process, our method yields a significantly faster and more accurate approach to document analysis.

The rapid growth in gravitational wave detections has spurred the need for comprehensive multimessenger astronomical and astrophysical research into neutron star mergers, particularly when involving neutron star-black hole (NSBH) pairs. A critical challenge in this field is addressing the vast computational demands of general relativistic hydrodynamics simulations required to predict the physical outcomes of NSBH mergers. To overcome this limitation, a novel approach combining dimensionality reduction and deep learning is proposed to categorize NSBH merger debris and determine accretion rates into forming black holes. By training on a extensive dataset consisting of 11,000 general relativistic numerical relativistic simulations, a deeply optimized model is developed to predict debris properties and forming black hole accretion rates with unprecedented accuracy. The results indicate a narrow range of frequencies for NSBH mergers, with associated variability in forming black hole frequencies and ejected masses. Furthermore, an elevated level of spin alignment between the NS and SBH is found to correspond to higher expected luminosities and ejected masses. These findings are discussed in the context of possible observational signatures across various channels.

Urban interactions are closely linked to economic activity and reflect societal living standards, yet they are influenced by individual diversity and limited theoretical understanding. COVID-19 the pandemic has been used as a natural experiment to investigate how the spread of disease in cities affects social interactions in daily life and how this varies across different populations. By combining mobile phone data with census data in Chengdu, China, we discovered that the pandemic significantly diminished mobility in the city, but there was significant variation among residents, with foreigners reducing their time in the city more than locals and lower-income individuals more than higher-income individuals. These disparities in interactions led to an increase in urban income inequality of about 1·1 percentage points, with the degree of inequality differing across various levels of city development. The study also found that the pandemic's impact on social interactions could be attributed to the elevated health risks associated with the virus.

Observations of young stellar objects by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array have shown that a significant number of early stellar formations involve the convergence of individual stellar systems with high levels of rotation and symmetry breaking.
Current theoretical models fail to accurately replicate this level of complexity in the early stages of low-mass star development.
In contrast, massive star formation models anticipate the accumulation of mass on a singular core through the accumulation of dense, collapsing gas clouds, a process that often results in the formation of massive star formations with multiple stellar systems.
However, there is a lack of evidence to support theories proposing that the individual components in these systems would merge, a statement that is especially striking given the high levels of violence and gas flows associated with their environments.
In order to examine the possibility of merges within these massive star formations with detailed gas simulations that incorporate radiative transfer effects, a scenario has been investigated in which three shells of gas have collapsed towards a central protostar with opposing linear velocities.
As a result of this complex environment, only a single merge was observed to combine a bound binary system with the central protostar, a process that occurred after a considerable time delay and was associated with high angular momentum.
The found merge rate appears to be a result of the peculiar linear geometry of gas flows in this particular simulation with a low level of symmetry, a statement that is expected to differ in more diverse and turbulent environments typically associated with massive star formations.

Recent research by Mansour, Shashank, and Zilberter explored the asymptotic behavior of weakly decaying, time-periodic water waves with complex vorticity patterns beneath the water's surface. For waves containing both Stokes and Kelvin waves, they derived an exact, explicit formula for the complex vorticity distribution in accordance with a given decay rate. Given this intricate relationship between vorticity distribution and surface elevation, obtaining a Hamiltonian for these waves requires solving a complex water-waves problem with evolving boundary conditions, a task for which we developed a new water-waves Hamiltonian involving both surface and subsurface variables. From this revised Hamiltonian, we were able to derive the corresponding equations of motion and their associated conservation laws. Furthermore, we were able to derive the corresponding Dystne equation in its full generality, which allowed us to non-perturbatively derive the deep-water wave frequency spectrum.

This paper introduces the concept of locally arching spaces and demonstrates how to define differential forms and vector fields on these spaces. Additionally, an integration theory for differential forms is presented, which includes an analogue of the Stokes theorem.

This work introduces a novel robotic navigation framework composed of two main components: a Stratified Navigation Controller (SNC) and an Obstacle Integration via Time To Collision (ITTC) module. The SNC innovates on traditional autonomous navigation by employing a hierarchical controller design tailored for complex scenarios. This approach enables the robot to grasp a wide array of navigation situations, on average dealing with convoluted environments via pre-set driving behaviors, and then executing safety maneuvers when facing imminent obstacles. Following this, the ITTC module optimizes real-time obstacle integration via dynamic velocity barriers, facilitating seamless incorporation of sonar data and generating a smooth barrier to avoid collisions. Our method demonstrates promising results in real-world experiments with an autonomous robotic vehicle, effectively managing diverse obstacles and delivering superior navigation performance compared to other advanced control strategies.

Deep-fakes and false news are becoming increasingly difficult to detect, posing a significant threat to society, and the spread of such content online accelerates due to the convenience of social media. This research proposes a hybrid method for identifying false news by combining contrasting backlinks and automated text condensation, focusing on the significance of URL domains and document complexity in the pursuit of more effective single-label classifiers. The results show that incorporating domain information leads to a 6.88% improvement over a baseline, while employing document simplification techniques results in a 5.85% increase in accuracy. The study presents a comprehensive analysis of the links between document complexity, domain reputation, and the propagation of false news, offering a foundation for the development of more nuanced misinformation detectors.

A mathematical investigation into the concept of curvature for linear operators within the framework of Gaussian random fields has yielded notable findings. Specifically, we establish that a positive or non-zero curvature guarantees a certain level of smoothness in a given probability field. Furthermore, we explore the operational significance of our main theorem in two distinct applications. First, we demonstrate an enhanced proof of a previous result concerning the differentiability of geostatistical variograms. Secondly, we examine the characteristics of common models used in applied settings, finding that a standard model known as the spherical model exhibits non-zero curvature, whereas another model called the cubic variogram displays zero curvature.

Finding a linearly convergent algorithm for evaluating the $\ell_1$-norm principal component under conditions of rotational symmetry has been made possible by an innovative mirror descent approach. This method employs a logarithmic norm as its regularization technique and achieves a convergence rate of $\Omega(d_\perp/\epsilon_\perp)$. Notably, our method offers the initial example of a mirror descent approach achieving a rate proportional to one, when aiming at a distant point outside the unit sphere within the unit ball of the $\ell_1$-norm.
